findings.text: non-blocking: the sentence states the discrete limbs are '7.1 % weaker ... at z = 0 and 13.6 % weaker at z = 0.6' at 8.11 m, but 7.1 % and 13.6 % are the vertical ratios at R = 6.672 m (0.9294 and 0.8636 in summary.json at discrete-limbs-011); at 8.11 m the deficits are 2.18 % and 6.74 %, which is what the table above correctly reports. The sentence is the one place the record states how much the criterion misses by at its near edge, so a reader is told the wrong margin for the wrong radius.

non-blocking: the 'median vertical difference' column (0.37 % and 2.02 %) is the median over all 53 sampled radii from 6.67 m, while the same row's 'median vertical ratio' (0.9973/0.9836) and 'radii within 2 %' (44 of 45, 26 of 45) are over the 45-radius criterion window, whose medians are 0.27 % and 1.64 %. Two cells of one row are computed over different sets, so the row cannot be read as one window statistic.
